jobs.title: Executive Director, California Youth & Government.
jobs.description:
The Opportunity For generations, California YMCA Youth & Government has helped young people discover the power of their voice, understand democracy through experience, and see themselves as leaders capable of shaping their communities and their future.
The Executive Director, California YMCA Youth & Government will provide strategic and executive leadership for one of the nation’s largest civic education and youth leadership programs, serving thousands of middle and high school students across California. Reporting to the Chief Program Officer of the YMCA of Metropolitan Los Angeles, the Executive Director will lead the next chapter of a statewide movement built on youth leadership, civic engagement, volunteer service, philanthropy, and the collective strength of YMCA associations throughout California.
This is an external-facing executive role requiring a leader who can build relationships and inspire investment in the mission. The Executive Director will cultivate donors and philanthropic partners, strengthen and develop the Board of Managers, engage and grow a statewide network of volunteers, build relationships with YMCA associations and civic and community leaders, and ensure the continued quality, relevance, reach, and sustainability of California YMCA Youth & Government.
At the same time, this leader will provide executive oversight for statewide programs including Model Legislature & Court (MLC), Model United Nations (MUN), national leadership experiences, and major conferences and events serving thousands of young people.
The successful candidate will understand that the strength of Youth & Government is not built by staff alone. It is built through people: young leaders, committed volunteers, engaged board members, donors, YMCA partners, educators, civic leaders, alumni, and communities united around a belief in the potential of young people.
The Leadership Mandate The next Executive Director will be charged with sustaining the extraordinary legacy of California YMCA Youth & Government while building the relationships, resources, leadership infrastructure, and strategy necessary for its future.
Three areas of executive leadership will be especially critical:
Philanthropy & Fund Development The Executive Director will serve as a chief fundraiser and relationship builder for California YMCA Youth & Government, leading a comprehensive development strategy with an annual goal of generating approximately $480,000 in philanthropic support.
This leader must be comfortable moving from strategy to solicitation. They will cultivate and steward individual donors, pursue major gifts, build corporate and foundation relationships, develop sponsorship opportunities, identify new sources of philanthropic revenue, and create meaningful opportunities for supporters to experience the impact of Youth & Government firsthand.
Just as importantly, the Executive Director will build a culture of philanthropy around the program, partnering with board members, volunteers, alumni, YMCA leaders, and other champions to expand the network of people willing to invest in its future.
Board Development & Governance The Executive Director will serve as the primary staff partner to the California YMCA Youth & Government Board of Managers, developing a highly engaged board that provides meaningful governance, strategic leadership, philanthropy, advocacy, and community influence.
The Executive Director will lead board recruitment, onboarding, engagement, development, and evaluation while partnering closely with board leadership to establish strategic priorities and measure progress.
The successful candidate will understand the difference between managing a board and developing one. We are seeking an executive who can build a strong partnership with volunteer governance leaders and help strengthen a board that is engaged, accountable, connected, and actively advancing the organization.
Volunteer Leadership & Development The Executive Director will lead a statewide volunteer engagement strategy that honors and retains the dedicated volunteers who have built and sustained this program while intentionally recruiting and developing the next generation of volunteer leaders.
This requires more than volunteer coordination. It requires an executive who understands volunteerism at the highest level and knows how to create an environment where people choose to give their time, expertise, relationships, and leadership year after year.
The Executive Director will strengthen the full volunteer experience, including recruitment, engagement, development, communication, recognition, leadership pathways, succession, and retention.
Statewide Leadership & Impact Beyond these three priorities, the Executive Director carries broad responsibility for the strategic direction, reputation, quality, and sustainability of California YMCA Youth & Government.
Provide executive oversight for statewide civic engagement and youth leadership programs, including Model Legislature & Court, Model United Nations, CONA, NJC, the National Youth Governors Conference, and other statewide and national experiences.
Lead government relations efforts for California YMCA Youth & Government, cultivating strategic relationships with elected officials, government agencies, policymakers, and civic leaders to strengthen the program’s visibility, advance its mission, and expand opportunities for youth civic engagement across California.
Provide strong fiscal stewardship through budgeting, forecasting, financial analysis, expense management, and long-term sustainability planning.

The Leader We Are Seeking We are seeking an accomplished, relationship-centered executive who believes deeply in the ability of young people to lead and understands how to translate mission into relationships, resources, and sustainable impact.
The strongest candidates will bring the executive presence to represent Youth & Government across California while also possessing the humility and relational leadership necessary to work effectively within a movement powered by volunteers, YMCA associations, board members, staff, and young people.
This leader should be equally comfortable meeting with a prospective major donor, partnering with a board chair, engaging a room of longtime volunteers, building relationships with civic and community leaders, coaching senior staff, reviewing financial performance, and listening to young people describe what they need from the program.
We are particularly interested in candidates who have demonstrated success in:
Fundraising and philanthropy, including personally cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding donors and developing sustainable sources of contributed revenue.
Board development and governance, with experience building productive partnerships with boards, committees, and volunteer governance structures.
Volunteer development, including recruiting, engaging, developing, recognizing, and retaining volunteers in organizations where volunteer leadership is integral to mission delivery.
Government relations and civic engagement, including building trusted relationships with elected officials, government agencies, civic leaders, and public sector partners to advance organizational priorities, strengthen visibility, and create opportunities for collaboration and impact.

Qualifications Candidates should bring a minimum of six to eight years of progressive leadership experience in nonprofit management, youth development, civic engagement, or a related field, with demonstrated experience in fundraising and resource development, board or volunteer governance, large-scale program or initiative leadership, volunteerism, government relations, and external partnership development.
A bachelor’s degree in public administration, political science, education, nonprofit management, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of academic preparation and experience, is expected. A master’s degree is preferred.
Experience within the YMCA movement or Youth & Government is valuable, but the ability to lead philanthropy, develop boards, mobilize volunteers, build relationships, and advance a complex statewide mission will be central to success.
A Statewide Leadership Opportunity California YMCA Youth & Government operates through a statewide network, and this Executive Director must be visible and engaged throughout California.
The position offers flexibility for the successful candidate to be based in Los Angeles or Sacramento, with frequent travel between both cities and throughout the state. The role requires participation in conferences, events, and program experiences that may occur during evenings and weekends, as well as regular overnight travel throughout the year. Overnight accommodation will vary based on the program or event and may include hotels, campgrounds, military installations, and other program-based settings.
This is a full-time executive position with a comprehensive YMCA benefits package, including health and well-being benefits, retirement benefits, professional development resources, and YMCA membership and program benefits.
About the YMCA of Metropolitan Los Angeles The YMCA of Metropolitan Los Angeles is the Center for Community Well-Being in Los Angeles, committed to strengthening communities by providing equitable programs and services that empower all. Through 29 YMCA Centers and more than 200 program sites across Los Angeles County, the LA Y works to advance equity in education, expand access to youth sports and healthy living, address food insecurity, create safe spaces for children and teens, and connect communities with critical health and well-being resources.
California YMCA Youth & Government extends that commitment across the state by giving young people opportunities to find their voice, understand civic institutions, practice leadership, build relationships across differences, and experience firsthand what it means to participate in democracy.

Reporting to the Vice President, Healthcare at Home and Post-Acute Services and partnering closely with the Chief Medical Officer, Hospital at Home, this leader oversees nursing operations, clinical operations, logistics, virtual care, workforce operations, vendor partnerships, and program administration across the HaH organization.

The Executive Director is accountable for operational excellence, patient and caregiver experience, regulatory compliance, workforce engagement, and financial performance. This leader will remain at the forefront of emerging models and best practices in home-based acute care delivery and serve as a national thought leader for HaH advancement. The Executive Director will serve as a key enterprise advocate for Hospital at Home innovation and best practices, helping expand access to care, improve patient outcomes and experience, optimize hospital capacity, and provide cost-effective alternatives to traditional inpatient care.

Strategic Leadership and Growth

• Identify and advance opportunities for program expansion, geographic growth, payer alignment, and operational scalability.
• Support enterprise strategies related to quality, experience, workforce engagement, growth, and financial sustainability.
• Serve as a leading voice – across the enterprise and externally – in advancing Hospital at Home operational innovation and industry partnerships.
• Monitor market trends, regulatory developments, and emerging operational best practices to strengthen program performance and positioning.

2. Program Design, Build and Implementation
• Oversee the design and development of the operational infrastructure and workflows required to support Hospital at Home services, including logistics, supply chain, virtual care operations, workforce deployment, and enabling technologies.
• Establish operational standards, service-level expectations, and vendor performance frameworks supporting acute care delivery in the home.
• Lead operational implementation and scaling of HaH capabilities across the enterprise.
• Partner with enterprise operational, digital, legal, regulatory, sourcing, and finance teams to support HaH performance, growth and sustainability.

3. Operational, Clinical, and Performance Leadership
• Provide executive oversight for HaH nursing, operational, and administrative functions, including intake, field operations, virtual care, and remote patient monitoring services.
• Lead operational integration between HaH and enterprise clinical and hospital-based services.
• Develop and support effective, efficient internal controls to ensure that policies and operating procedures are followed.
• Oversee workforce planning, operational workflows, resource deployment, and capacity management across the HaH organization.
• Develop high-performing teams and foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, innovation, and service excellence.
• Oversee the HaH virtual command center and related operational support functions.
• Lead continuous improvement initiatives focused on operational effectiveness, service quality, regulatory readiness, and scalability.
• Analyze operational workflows and procedures and identify and implement continuous improvement opportunities.
• Ensure that the voice of the patient – and their caregiver – is represented and persists throughout HaH care delivery and services.

4. Financial Management
• Partner with finance and executive leadership to develop and manage operating and capital budgets for the HaH organization.
• Monitor operational and financial variances and performance metrics and implement corrective actions as needed.
• Support forecasting, resource planning, and financial optimization strategies aligned with organizational goals.

5.Stakeholder Engagement
• Serve as a key operational leader and change agent in advancing HaH adoption across the enterprise.
• Build strong partnerships across clinical, operation, and administrative teams to support successful program integration and growth.
• Promote alignment, engagement, and communication among internal and external stakeholders supporting HaH services.

QUALIFICATIONS

• Demonstrated experience managing operational, quality, and financial performance in a healthcare environment

PREFERRED EXPERIENCE

• Experience developing or scaling innovative care delivery models

new_jobs.description:
The Opportunity For generations, California YMCA Youth & Government has helped young people discover the power of their voice, understand democracy through experience, and see themselves as leaders capable of shaping their communities and their future.
The Executive Director, California YMCA Youth & Government will provide strategic and executive leadership for one of the nation’s largest civic education and youth leadership programs, serving thousands of middle and high school students across California. Reporting to the Chief Program Officer of the YMCA of Metropolitan Los Angeles, the Executive Director will lead the next chapter of a statewide movement built on youth leadership, civic engagement, volunteer service, philanthropy, and the collective strength of YMCA associations throughout California.
This is an external-facing executive role requiring a leader who can build relationships and inspire investment in the mission. The Executive Director will cultivate donors and philanthropic partners, strengthen and develop the Board of Managers, engage and grow a statewide network of volunteers, build relationships with YMCA associations and civic and community leaders, and ensure the continued quality, relevance, reach, and sustainability of California YMCA Youth & Government.
At the same time, this leader will provide executive oversight for statewide programs including Model Legislature & Court (MLC), Model United Nations (MUN), national leadership experiences, and major conferences and events serving thousands of young people.
The successful candidate will understand that the strength of Youth & Government is not built by staff alone. It is built through people: young leaders, committed volunteers, engaged board members, donors, YMCA partners, educators, civic leaders, alumni, and communities united around a belief in the potential of young people.
The Leadership Mandate The next Executive Director will be charged with sustaining the extraordinary legacy of California YMCA Youth & Government while building the relationships, resources, leadership infrastructure, and strategy necessary for its future.
Three areas of executive leadership will be especially critical:
Philanthropy & Fund Development The Executive Director will serve as a chief fundraiser and relationship builder for California YMCA Youth & Government, leading a comprehensive development strategy with an annual goal of generating approximately $480,000 in philanthropic support.
This leader must be comfortable moving from strategy to solicitation. They will cultivate and steward individual donors, pursue major gifts, build corporate and foundation relationships, develop sponsorship opportunities, identify new sources of philanthropic revenue, and create meaningful opportunities for supporters to experience the impact of Youth & Government firsthand.
Just as importantly, the Executive Director will build a culture of philanthropy around the program, partnering with board members, volunteers, alumni, YMCA leaders, and other champions to expand the network of people willing to invest in its future.
Board Development & Governance The Executive Director will serve as the primary staff partner to the California YMCA Youth & Government Board of Managers, developing a highly engaged board that provides meaningful governance, strategic leadership, philanthropy, advocacy, and community influence.
The Executive Director will lead board recruitment, onboarding, engagement, development, and evaluation while partnering closely with board leadership to establish strategic priorities and measure progress.
The successful candidate will understand the difference between managing a board and developing one. We are seeking an executive who can build a strong partnership with volunteer governance leaders and help strengthen a board that is engaged, accountable, connected, and actively advancing the organization.
Volunteer Leadership & Development The Executive Director will lead a statewide volunteer engagement strategy that honors and retains the dedicated volunteers who have built and sustained this program while intentionally recruiting and developing the next generation of volunteer leaders.
This requires more than volunteer coordination. It requires an executive who understands volunteerism at the highest level and knows how to create an environment where people choose to give their time, expertise, relationships, and leadership year after year.
The Executive Director will strengthen the full volunteer experience, including recruitment, engagement, development, communication, recognition, leadership pathways, succession, and retention.
Statewide Leadership & Impact Beyond these three priorities, the Executive Director carries broad responsibility for the strategic direction, reputation, quality, and sustainability of California YMCA Youth & Government.
Provide executive oversight for statewide civic engagement and youth leadership programs, including Model Legislature & Court, Model United Nations, CONA, NJC, the National Youth Governors Conference, and other statewide and national experiences.
Lead government relations efforts for California YMCA Youth & Government, cultivating strategic relationships with elected officials, government agencies, policymakers, and civic leaders to strengthen the program’s visibility, advance its mission, and expand opportunities for youth civic engagement across California.
Provide strong fiscal stewardship through budgeting, forecasting, financial analysis, expense management, and long-term sustainability planning.

The Leader We Are Seeking We are seeking an accomplished, relationship-centered executive who believes deeply in the ability of young people to lead and understands how to translate mission into relationships, resources, and sustainable impact.
The strongest candidates will bring the executive presence to represent Youth & Government across California while also possessing the humility and relational leadership necessary to work effectively within a movement powered by volunteers, YMCA associations, board members, staff, and young people.
This leader should be equally comfortable meeting with a prospective major donor, partnering with a board chair, engaging a room of longtime volunteers, building relationships with civic and community leaders, coaching senior staff, reviewing financial performance, and listening to young people describe what they need from the program.
We are particularly interested in candidates who have demonstrated success in:
Fundraising and philanthropy, including personally cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding donors and developing sustainable sources of contributed revenue.
Board development and governance, with experience building productive partnerships with boards, committees, and volunteer governance structures.
Volunteer development, including recruiting, engaging, developing, recognizing, and retaining volunteers in organizations where volunteer leadership is integral to mission delivery.
Government relations and civic engagement, including building trusted relationships with elected officials, government agencies, civic leaders, and public sector partners to advance organizational priorities, strengthen visibility, and create opportunities for collaboration and impact.

Qualifications Candidates should bring a minimum of six to eight years of progressive leadership experience in nonprofit management, youth development, civic engagement, or a related field, with demonstrated experience in fundraising and resource development, board or volunteer governance, large-scale program or initiative leadership, volunteerism, government relations, and external partnership development.
A bachelor’s degree in public administration, political science, education, nonprofit management, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of academic preparation and experience, is expected. A master’s degree is preferred.
Experience within the YMCA movement or Youth & Government is valuable, but the ability to lead philanthropy, develop boards, mobilize volunteers, build relationships, and advance a complex statewide mission will be central to success.
A Statewide Leadership Opportunity California YMCA Youth & Government operates through a statewide network, and this Executive Director must be visible and engaged throughout California.
The position offers flexibility for the successful candidate to be based in Los Angeles or Sacramento, with frequent travel between both cities and throughout the state. The role requires participation in conferences, events, and program experiences that may occur during evenings and weekends, as well as regular overnight travel throughout the year. Overnight accommodation will vary based on the program or event and may include hotels, campgrounds, military installations, and other program-based settings.
This is a full-time executive position with a comprehensive YMCA benefits package, including health and well-being benefits, retirement benefits, professional development resources, and YMCA membership and program benefits.
About the YMCA of Metropolitan Los Angeles The YMCA of Metropolitan Los Angeles is the Center for Community Well-Being in Los Angeles, committed to strengthening communities by providing equitable programs and services that empower all. Through 29 YMCA Centers and more than 200 program sites across Los Angeles County, the LA Y works to advance equity in education, expand access to youth sports and healthy living, address food insecurity, create safe spaces for children and teens, and connect communities with critical health and well-being resources.
California YMCA Youth & Government extends that commitment across the state by giving young people opportunities to find their voice, understand civic institutions, practice leadership, build relationships across differences, and experience firsthand what it means to participate in democracy.

new_jobs.description:
The Naresh K. Vashisht College of Medicine at Texas A&M University (TAMU) invites applications for one (1) Clinical or Instructional Academic Professional Track (Non-Tenure) position for a full-time, 11-month appointment with an anticipated start date of October 2026. Applications will be considered for titles of Clinical Assistant Professor, Clinical Associate Professor, Clinical Professor commensurate with qualifications.

Responsibilities for this position as a faculty member include:

The Campus Executive Director, San Antonio campus is a critical leadership position at Vashisht College of Medicine, responsible for leading and directing the education and administrative operations of the college’s San Antonio campus. The Campus Executive Director (CED) serves as the point of contact for academic and administrative operations for the San Antonio campus of the Texas A&M University Naresh K. Vashisht College of Medicine. This role is the point of contact for all aspects of medical education (UME, GME, graduate studies), faculty affairs, research, student affairs/services, clinical partnerships, and community engagement for the region. The CED will work collaboratively with main campus and centralized offices/leadership to ensure alignment. The CED ensures the delivery of high-quality medical education aligned with the mission, vision, and values of the Vashisht College of Medicine and compliant with accreditation standards.

Key Responsibilities:

Academic Leadership:
Provide academic and administrative leadership for the San Antonio campus, ensuring high-quality medical education aligned with VCOM's mission, with specific oversight of rural medicine initiatives, curriculum implementation, faculty engagement, and community partnerships.
Provide leadership and operational implemention/oversight for the San Antonio campus that aligns with the mission and strategic plan of the Central Texas region.
Collaborate with main campus leadership to implement and assess curriculum, educational policies, and assessment tools.
Promote academic excellence and innovation in teaching, learning, and student performance.

Faculty and Staff Development:
Recruit, appoint, and evaluate faculty and administrative staff.
Support faculty development, mentorship, and promotion processes.
Foster a culture of collaboration, and academic integrity.

Student Affairs:
In collaboration with the main campus and local student affairs leadership, oversee student advising, wellness programs, academic progress, and career development.
Serve as a liaison between students and the main campus for academic and administrative matters.
Promote a safe and supportive learning environment.

Clinical and Community Partnerships in the San Antonio region:
Develop and maintain strong relationships with affiliated hospitals, health systems, clinics, and community partners.
Ensure adequate and high-quality clinical training opportunities for medical students.
Represent the school in local healthcare, educational, and civic communities.

Accreditation and Compliance:
Ensure campus operations comply with LCME accreditation standards and institutional policies.
Participate in self-study processes and site visits.
Maintain documentation and continuous quality improvement measures.

Budget and Operations:
Develop and manage the campus budget in alignment with institutional goals.
Oversee campus facilities, resources, and administrative functions.

Information about Texas A&M University can be found online here: https://www.tamu.edu/about/index.html.

Together, Texas A&M University, Texas A&M Health, and the Naresh K. Vashisht College of Medicine are working to improve healthcare through transformative education, innovative research, and team-based care delivery.
